answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The result is a self-purifying economy: every epoch, low-cost fake identities are filtered out by the same reputation mechanics that reward the honest ones.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a vine as the anchor of the cost. A dune stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a meadow...
